raw_response:
I have been working this land for 45 years, so I know what each crop needs here in Quzhou. Our soil is alright but it has been tired from the wheat-maize rotation, so I pay attention to balance the nutrients, not just throw on more urea like some neighbors do.

I have 9 mu total. I keep 6 mu in the wheat-maize double crop because that is our staple income — wheat in winter, maize in summer right after harvest. The other 3 mu I plant cotton because the price has been workable and cotton handles our drier patch better. With only 2 people in the household and me being 63, I cannot manage too much cotton — it needs hand picking.

For wheat, I sow improved varieties like Jimai 22 in early October. I apply about 15 kg/mu of compound fertilizer (N-P-K roughly 15-15-15) as base, then top-dress 12 kg/mu of urea at jointing in March. That gives me roughly 22 kg N, 9 kg P, 9 kg K per mu. I irrigate from my well 3 times — at green-up, jointing, and grain-filling. I expect 500 kg/mu in a good year.

For maize, I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid right after wheat harvest. I apply 20 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K per mu, mostly as compound at sowing plus urea at big-trumpet stage. Summer rain usually covers most water needs, so I only irrigate once or twice if July is dry. I expect 550 kg/mu.

For cotton, I use a Bt hybrid because bollworm is too costly to spray for otherwise. I apply 18 kg N, 9 kg P, 10 kg K per mu — cotton needs more potassium for boll development. I irrigate twice and spray 4 times for aphids and mirid bugs. I expect 250 kg/mu of seed cotton.

I would rather spend a little extra on fertilizer than watch yield drop. Pesticide I am more careful with — I only spray when I see the pest.
